CANTONMENT AREAS UNION COMMITTEES SERVANTS CONDUCT RULES; 1966
CANTONMENT AREAS UNION COMMITTEES SERVANTS CONDUCT RULES;
1966
[Gazette of Pakistan, Part
III, 30th September, 1966]
No. 1947/66.---In exercise of the powers conferred by Article 89 of
the Basic Democracies Order, 1959 (P.O. 18 of 1959), read with item 13 of the
Sixth Schedule thereto, the Central Government is pleased to make the following
rules, namely:--‑
1. Short title, application and commencement.---(1) These rules may
be called the Cantonment Areas Union Committees Servants Conduct Rules, 1966.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
(3) They apply to all Union
Committee Servants, whether on duty, leave or in foreign service.
2. Definitions.---In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,
the following expressions shall have the meanings hereby respectively assigned
to them, that is to say:--
(a) "Government"
means the Central Government;
(b) "Union
Committee servant" means a servant of a Union Committee: and
(c) "Union
Committee servant's family" includes---
(i) his wife
children or step-children whether residing with the Union Committee servant or
not; and
(ii) any other
relative of his or his wife when residing with him, but does not include a wife
legally separated from the Union Committee servant or a child or step-child who
is no longer in any way dependent upon him or of whose custody the Union
Committee servant has been deprived of by law.
3. Gifts.---Save as otherwise provided in this rule, no Union
Committee servant shall, except with the previous sanction of the Controlling
Authority, accept or permit any member of his family to accept, from any person
any gift the receipt of which will place him under any form of official
obligation to the donor, the decision of the Controlling Authority thereon
shall be final.
4. Public demonstration in honour of Union Committee Servants.---(1)
Save as otherwise provided in this rule, no Union Committee servant shall,
except with the previous sanction of the Controlling Authority:---
(a) receive any
complimentary or validictory address, except any testimonial or attend any
meeting or entertainment held in his honour;
or
(b) take part in
the presentation of a complimentary or valedictory address or a testimonial to
any other Union Committee servant, or any person who has recently quitted, the
service of the Union Committee or attend a meeting or entertainment held in
honour of such other Union servant or person.
(2) Notwithstanding anything
contained in sub-rule (1):--‑
(a) a Union
Committee servant may, at the request of any public body, sit for portrait,
bust or statue not intended for presentation to him:
(b) subject to
the provisions of any general or special order of the Government or the
Controlling Authority, a Union Committee servant may take part in the raising
of a fund to be presented in recognition of the service of any other Union
Committee servant or of a person, who has recently quitted the service of Union
Committee or the foundation of a scholarship or any other public or charitable object or on the execution of any portrait,
bust or statute not intended for presentation to such other Union Committee
servant or person; and
(c) subject to
the provisions of any general or special order of the Government or the
Controlling Authority, a Union Committee servant may attend a farewell
entertainment of a substantially private and informal character held in honour
of himself or any other Union Committee servant or any person who has recently
quitted the service of the Union Committee on the occasion of the retirement
from service or department from the Union Committee of himself or such other
Union Committee servant or person.
